clue.text: Fish haul brought in ray without tail

indicators.note: says the haul word is put inside the shortened ray word
says the last letter of the synonym for ray is cut off

parts.note: a ray of light is a beam
to lug is to haul or drag

explanation.surface: A fisherman pulls in a catch that includes a ray missing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ray' is a beam of light here, not a fish; 'without tail' leaves BEA, and 'brought in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga is a large sturgeon, prized for its caviar.

clue.text: It's most suitable when catching just a bit of sleeping?

definitions.text: It's most suitable when catching just a bit of sleeping?

parts.words: It's most suitable when catching just a bit of sleeping?
parts.note: a bed frame is the ideal place for grabbing a little sleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'catching just a bit of sleeping' suggests a nap, but the thing meant is what you sleep on.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedstead is the framework of a bed, the furniture on which one sleeps.

clue.text: Lion going round lush hot country in Africa

indicators.note: the lion's name surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Leo is the Lion of the zodiac
a lush is a drunkard, a sot
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A lion circles a drunk in a hot African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small mountain kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Present sex in the past as experiment?

parts.note: to present is to give
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to having tried sex once, long ago, as an experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a go is to try it out, attempting it to see what happens.

clue.text: Finishes article about senior officer of a religious area

indicators.note: here the word for finishes goes around the officer's abbreviation

parts.note: something that finishes dies away or ends
OC stands for Officer Commanding
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A senior officer is put in charge of a religious district and its affairs wind up.
explanation.walkthrough: OC (Officer Commanding) is an army abbreviation; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocese is a bishop's district, so the adjective describes anything belonging to that church area.

clue.text: Organised pic with son and relation having guardianship role

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are organised into a new order

explanation.surface: A photo is arranged showing a son with a relative who looks after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in the place of a parent, describing someone with a guardian's responsibilities.

clue.text: Complain about foul when hacked down

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: the foul word has its last letter chopped off

parts.note: vile means foul

explanation.surface: A footballer protests about a foul after being brought down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacked down' trims VILE to VIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavil is to raise petty objections, to quibble.

clue.text: One weeping to see 50 on board slaver

indicators.note: the numeral is taken aboard inside the weeping word

parts.note: someone who sobs is a sobber
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A captive weeps to see fifty people aboard a slave ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slaver' looks like a slave ship but is the verb meaning to drool.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaver is to let saliva run from the mouth, to drool.

clue.text: Almost, but not quite, round number? That's tidy

indicators.note: the almost word is not quite complete, so its last letter goes

parts.note: near means almost
ten is a round number

explanation.surface: Someone describes a figure that is nearly but not exactly a round number as tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not quite' trims NEAR to NEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten something is to make it neater, to tidy it up.

clue.text: Argument with everybody blocks someone broadcasting circus act

indicators.note: the other pieces sit inside and block the sower word

parts.note: a sower broadcasts, or scatters, seed
to have words is to argue
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A row breaks out and everyone shouts down a radio presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcasting' suggests radio, but here it means scattering seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sword-swallowing is a traditional circus and sideshow performance.

clue.text: Carry out recall of legislation about working of visa denial

indicators.note: the doing word goes round the rearranged visa letters

parts.note: to carry out a task is to do it

indicators.note: the letters of visa are worked into a new order
recall here means calling back, so the word for legislation is read backwards

parts.note: legislation is law

explanation.surface: A government repeals a law about how visa refusals are handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry out recall of legislation' reads like repealing a law, but splits into three jobs: 'working of' signals the anagram, 'about' the container, and 'recall of' the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A disavowal is a refusal to acknowledge something, a form of denial.

clue.text: Shakespearean heroine mostly quick to embrace love, on reflection

indicators.note: the whole construction is read backwards, as in a mirror
the shortened word wraps around the letter for love
the last letter of the living word is dropped

parts.note: quick has the old sense living, as in the quick and the dead
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare heroine is eager to take love in, when she thinks about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick' means living (ALIVE); 'mostly' gives ALIV, 'to embrace' adds O to make ALOIV, and 'on reflection' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Viola is the heroine of Twelfth Night, who disguises herself as Cesario.

clue.text: Row about a vacated tenement looking increasingly shabby

indicators.note: the row word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters of tenement remain

explanation.surface: A row of empty tenements is getting ever more run-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacated' means emptied of its middle; 'about' signals the container; 'looking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby and worn, so the comparative form means more shabby.

clue.text: Concern about politician's ability

indicators.note: the word for concern surrounds the politician

parts.note: concern means care
Lib is short for a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: People worry about whether a politician is up to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Calibre means the quality or standard of someone's talent, a measure of their worth.

clue.text: Subtle quality of a city according to locals

parts.note: Italians call their capital city Roma

explanation.surface: Residents say their city has some special, hard-to-pin-down character.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma can mean a pervasive subtle quality or atmosphere, beyond its literal sense of a smell.

clue.text: Hard mineral perhaps unexpectedly cracked open by one

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are split to let the numeral in
the letters of perhaps come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A hard rock might surprisingly be split open by a single blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges PERHAPS to SAPPHRE, and 'cracked open by' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapphire is a gem variety of corundum, one of the hardest natural minerals.

clue.text: Given job around sick ward, being determined

indicators.note: the employment word goes around the rearranged ward letters

parts.note: someone given a job is hired

indicators.note: the letters of ward are sick, so they come out disordered

explanation.surface: A new hire is set to work on a hospital ward, full of resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' signals the anagram (ARDW), and 'around' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that is hard-wired is fixed by nature, determined in advance.

clue.text: Criminal group's protecting racket set up in island

indicators.note: the gang surrounds the reversed racket word

parts.note: a triad is a Chinese criminal gang

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, reversed

parts.note: a din is a racket, a loud noise

explanation.surface: A gang runs a protection racket on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses in a down clue, giving NID; 'protecting' signals the container, playing on a protection racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinidad is the larger of the two islands of Trinidad and Tobago in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Base returned broadcasting with style

indicators.note: the base word is turned round

parts.note: a bed is a base, as a flower bed or river bed
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A presenter goes back to the studio base and broadcasts with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns BED into DEB.
explanation.definitionFit: A debonair person is suave and confident, someone who carries themselves stylishly.

clue.text: No longer big enough for instance

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so
ample means sufficient, big enough

explanation.surface: Clothing that is no longer roomy enough, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a single case representing a type, a specimen.

clue.text: Happen again on short cut

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: the last letter of the brusque word is dropped

parts.note: curt means cut short, brusque

explanation.surface: Something keeps happening because of a quick shortcut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims CURT to CUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to occur again or repeatedly.

clue.text: Caught? Run out? Yours truly being dismissed in restrained game

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

indicators.note: the setter's pronoun is sent out of the restrained word

parts.note: quiet means restrained or subdued
yours truly is the setter, I

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary: caught, run out, the speaker dismissed in a low-key match.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket terms mislead: the game is played with mallets and hoops on a lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Croquet is a lawn sport in which players hit wooden balls through hoops with mallets.

clue.text: Fixed problem with radio

definitions.meaning: crackling interference heard on a radio

explanation.surface: Someone says the radio fault has been mended.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means motionless, and it is also the noise caused by atmospheric electrical interference.

clue.text: Teacher's first reprimand — may leave child this?

indicators.note: the first letter of the teacher's word is taken

parts.note: an earful is a scolding

explanation.surface: A teacher's opening telling-off might leave a pupil close to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: A scolded child may end up weepy, on the verge of crying.

clue.text: Discussion group supporting doubtful response?

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting
um is a hesitant reply

explanation.surface: A panel backs an answer that sounds unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a meeting or medium where ideas are exchanged and debated.

clue.text: View of satellite? No sign, looking back around West

indicators.note: the backward letters go around the abbreviation for West
the two words are read backwards together

parts.note: no taken as written
an omen is a sign

explanation.surface: An astronomer sees no sign of the moon when looking back towards the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking back' gives NEMOON, and 'around' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The new moon is the lunar phase seen at the start of its cycle, a view of Earth's satellite.

clue.text: Narrow backing for programme already shown (though no duplication)

indicators.note: one of the doubled letters is removed so none is duplicated
backing means turning back, so the programme word is read backwards

parts.note: a repeat is a programme shown again

explanation.surface: A TV schedule shrinks its support for reruns, though without copying any.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing for' turns REPEAT into TAEPER; 'though no duplication' removes one of the two Es.
explanation.definitionFit: To taper is to narrow gradually towards one end.

clue.text: In which one collects drinks provided by parliamentary official

indicators.note: the drinks come after the official

parts.note: a whip enforces party discipline in Parliament
a round is a set of drinks bought for a group

explanation.surface: A party enforcer buys a round at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament a whip keeps party members voting in line.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip-round is an informal collection of money from a group, for a gift or a cause.

clue.text: Blubber sandwiches European exhibited with half-American dairy business

indicators.note: the crying word holds the other letters between its own

parts.note: to blubber is to cry

indicators.note: the first half of the word American is taken

explanation.surface: Whale fat is packed with a European product shown alongside an American one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blubber' is the verb to weep, not whale fat; 'half' takes four letters, and 'sandwiches' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamery is a business that makes or sells butter, cheese and other milk products.

clue.text: Revised and cut down, putting third item first

indicators.note: the third letter of the dieting word goes to the front

parts.note: someone who has dieted has cut down on food

explanation.surface: A list was revised and trimmed by moving the third item to the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The E in third place in DIETED moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An edited text has been revised and corrected before publication.
